subject: how to arrange an omnibus test of the equality of covariance matrices across groups

messages.author: dd7b6386820f0eab
messages.subject: how to arrange an omnibus test of the equality of covariance matrices across groups
parts:
Hi,
I'm testing a multiple-group cfa model (two independent sample) and my main objective is to test the invariance of the model across the two samples. Is it possible with lavaan to perform an omnibus test of covariance matrices  (i.e., Σg = Σg′) as suggested by Vandenberg, & Lance, (2000, pp. 12, option (a)) ?
Thank you

References
Vandenberg, & Lance, (2000). A review and synthesis of the measurement invariance literature: Suggestions, practices, and recommendations for organizational research. Organizational Research Methods, 2, 4-69.

On 09/19/2012 06:39 PM, fabio presaghi wrote:
> Hi,
> I'm testing a multiple-group cfa model (two independent sample) and my
> main objective is to test the invariance of the model across the two
> samples. Is it possible with lavaan to perform an omnibus test of
> covariance matrices (i.e., Σg = Σg′) as suggested byVandenberg, &

> Lance, (2000, pp. 12, option (a)) ?
> Thank you
>
> References
> Vandenberg, & Lance, (2000). A review and synthesis of the measurement
> invariance literature: Suggestions, practices, and recommendations for

> organizational research. /Organizational Research Methods/, 2, 4-69.

This is simply Box's M test for equal covariances, right? There is no
canned function to do just this in lavaan (maybe in other packages?). Of
course, you could do it manually: specify a model with only variances
and covariances, and constrain them to be equal across groups. For the
Holzinger & Swineford model, this would be something like:


HS.model.BOX.M <- ' x1 ~~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
x2 ~~ x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
x3 ~~ x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
x4 ~~ x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
x5 ~~ x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
x6 ~~ x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
x7 ~~ x7 + x8 + x9
x8 ~~ x8 + x9
x9 ~~ x9
'

fit <- cfa(HS.model.BOX.M, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
meanstructure=FALSE,
group.equal=c("residuals", "residual.covariances"))
summary(fit)


(the terms 'residuals' and 'residual.covariances' in the group.equal
argument seem a bit odd here; I may provide the aliases 'ov.variances'
and 'ov.covariances' in a future release)

Yves.
